name: Duloxetine
route_note: Oral delayed-release (enteric-coated) capsules once or twice daily.

discovery.by: Eli Lilly (David Robertson, David Wong and colleagues)
discovery.note: A thiophene naphthyloxy propylamine developed at Lilly in the late 1980s as a balanced serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor.

tagline: SNRI approved for depression, anxiety and several chronic pain conditions
summary: Duloxetine is a balanced serotonin–noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor approved for depression, generalised anxiety disorder and chronic pain conditions including diabetic neuropathic pain and fibromyalgia. In Europe it is also licensed for stress urinary incontinence.
mechanism: Duloxetine potently inhibits both serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake. Enhancement of descending inhibitory serotonergic and noradrenergic pain pathways in the spinal cord is thought to underlie its analgesic effect, independent of mood improvement.
In the sacral spinal cord (Onuf's nucleus) increased serotonin and noradrenaline enhance pudendal nerve activity and urethral sphincter tone, the basis of its use in stress urinary incontinence.
uses: Chronic musculoskeletal pain (osteoarthritis, low back pain)
Stress urinary incontinence in women (EU, Yentreve)

history.title: Approvals
history.detail: The FDA approves Cymbalta for depression and diabetic neuropathic pain; the EU approves Yentreve for stress urinary incontinence.

history.title: GAD
history.detail: Duloxetine is approved in the US for generalised anxiety disorder.

history.title: Fibromyalgia
history.detail: The FDA approves duloxetine for fibromyalgia.

history.title: Musculoskeletal pain
history.detail: Approval for chronic musculoskeletal pain, including osteoarthritis and chronic low back pain.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: US generic duloxetine launches in December 2013.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP1A2 and CYP2D6; moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor

safety.boxed_warning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours in children, adolescents and young adults (under 25) taking antidepressants; monitor for clinical worsening.

facts: Duloxetine was one of the first antidepressants approved specifically for a neuropathic pain indication.
